I actually just started learning yesterday too; I mean, I got pretty good in a short amount of time though and didn't alternate between feet. I just kept them together and jumped using my calves and glutes and the front bottom part of my foot.

Since I'm new, I did this:

Jumped 25 times until I felt like I got it right, then jumped to 50 in a row, then 100, then 150. I went down from there, and it took me about an hour or so, so say:

Warmed up with a typical stretch.

Then 25 jumps with about a 20-second rest in between; did this for about 10 minutes.

Then jumped up to 50 jumps with again about a 20-second rest for about 15 minutes.

Then jumped up to 100 jumps in a row with about a 30-second rest for about 15 minutes.

Then jumped to 150 jumps with a 30-second rest in between each. Did that for the rest of the time until I was super tired, so I did that for about 20-25 minutes.

Then I cooled down by doing 100 twice, then 50 three times, then 25 four times each with their respective wait times.

Just do about an hour and jump when you can, but make sure you jump every time to where your calves hurt.
